scenario: A hospital analytics team studies post-operative length of stay, but the warehouse records only stays longer than 7 days because short discharges remain in a separate transactional system. The team wants the mean stay across all patients.

data.description: Only stays greater than 7 days are present in the warehouse. Length of stay is modeled as Normal with known standard deviation sigma = 3 days.

question: Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean length of stay mu across all surgical patients and (b) the fraction of all patients represented in the warehouse.
naive_answer: The average stay is about 8.6 days because that is the warehouse average.
naive_trap: The warehouse excludes short stays entirely, so the observed mean reflects only a truncated upper tail.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: Solve 8.5754 = mu + 3*lambda((7-mu)/3). Step 2: The solution has alpha about 1.0, so mu = 7 - 3 = 4 days. Step 3: The represented fraction is sf(1.0) about 0.1587.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu):
    a=(7-mu)/3
    return mu + 3*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a) - 8.5754
mu=brentq(eq,-20,6.99)
frac=norm.sf((7-mu)/3)
assert abs(mu-4.0)<0.1 and abs(frac-0.1587)<0.005
